ab_still_unreached_root_cause: opportunity_value is now correctly distributed (10 HIGH / 22 MEDIUM / 8 LOW across the 40 real vacancies, vs 40/40 LOW before the fix), and PRIORITY_APPLY is proven reachable in isolation (test_realistic_employer_score_makes_priority_apply_reachable). However A/B remains 0/40 in this real sample because a separate, higher-precedence, NOT-yet-fixed gate (Tier 2: 'at least one mandatory factual requirement has no verified evidence') fires on 32/40 (80%) of real vacancies and routes them to HUMAN_REVIEW before opportunity_value is ever consulted at Tier 5. This is Task 21.15's calibration finding #2 (incomplete behavioural-marker list), intentionally NOT touched in this task per its explicit scope.
measurement_caveat: Re-running the real ApplicationService.evaluate_job() pipeline against the same 40 vacancies made fresh OpenAI calls (analyze_job + employer.analyze), which are not perfectly deterministic even at temperature=0. 14/40 (35%) vacancies show some drift in a dimension NOT touched by this fix (vacancy_validity, hard_eligibility inputs, candidate_competitiveness, screening_decision, or ats_grade) between the BEFORE and AFTER runs, and both of the 2 priority-level changes are attributable to this AI-call variance (confirmed by inspecting requirement_evidence_summary), not to the opportunity_value fix. The fix's effect is best isolated via the opportunity_value field itself (deterministically caused by this change) and via the dedicated unit tests.
